name: dotnet-msix

Packages MSIX apps: creation, signing, Store submission, App Installer sideload/auto-update, enterprise deployment, bundles, CI/CD. Assumptions: Windows App SDK 1.6+, .NET 8.0+, Windows 10 build 19041+ for MSIX with Windows App SDK; build 1709+ for App Installer auto-update.

WinUI 3/Windows App SDK apps can package directly from `.csproj` (`WindowsPackageType`); WPF/WinForms use a Visual Studio “Windows Application Packaging Project” `.wapproj` referencing the app project. See [skill:dotnet-winui] for WinUI setup/packaging mode, [skill:dotnet-native-aot] for AOT + MSIX, [skill:dotnet-gha-patterns] and [skill:dotnet-ado-patterns] for CI/CD, [skill:dotnet-nuget-authoring] for NuGet, [skill:dotnet-containers] for containers. More: [references/detailed-examples.md](references/detailed-examples.md).

Build:
dotnet publish --configuration Release --runtime win-x64 \

All MSIX packages must be signed to install on Windows. The signing certificate's Subject must match the `Publisher` attribute in the package manifest.

Development self-signed certificate:
$cert = New-SelfSignedCertificate `
-Subject "CN=My Company, O=My Company, L=Seattle, S=WA, C=US" `
-FriendlyName "MyApp Dev Signing" `
-CertStoreLocation "Cert:\CurrentUser\My" `
-TextExtension @("<REDACTED_IP>={text}<REDACTED_IP>.<REDACTED_IP>.3", `
"<REDACTED_IP>={text}")
$password = ConvertTo-SecureString -String "$env:CERT_PASSWORD" -Force -AsPlainText
Export-PfxCertificate -Cert $cert `
-FilePath "MyApp_DevSigning.pfx" `
$signtool = Get-ChildItem "C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\bin\*\x64\signtool.exe" |
Sort-Object { [version]($_.Directory.Parent.Name) } -Descending |
Select-Object -First 1 -ExpandProperty FullName
& $signtool sign /fd SHA256 /a /f "MyApp_DevSigning.pfx" `
/p "$env:CERT_PASSWORD" `
"AppPackages\MyApp_1.0.0.0_x64.msix"

Production direct distribution: obtain a trusted CA code-signing certificate; Subject must match the `Publisher` in `Package.appxmanifest`; timestamp the signature for long-term validity.
& signtool.exe sign /fd SHA256 /sha1 "THUMBPRINT_HERE" `
/tr http://timestamp.digicert.com /td SHA256 `
"AppPackages\MyApp_1.0.0.0_x64.msix"
& signtool.exe sign /fd SHA256 /f "production-cert.pfx" `
/p "$env:CERT_PASSWORD" `
/tr http://timestamp.digicert.com /td SHA256 `
"AppPackages\MyApp_1.0.0.0_x64.msix"

Store: register at https://partner.microsoft.com/dashboard, reserve app name, build with Store association, submit `.msixupload` through Partner Center. Microsoft validates, signs, publishes, and re-signs Store apps with a Microsoft-issued certificate. No production signing certificate is needed for Store-only distribution. Development uses a test certificate; self-signed certs require manual install, enterprise certs can be deployed via Group Policy, direct downloads require trusted CA signing.

App Installer `.appinstaller` supports direct distribution and auto-updates; host on web server, network share, or CDN. Install via:
ms-appinstaller:?source=https://mycompany.com/apps/MyApp.appinstaller

Enterprise options: Microsoft Intune, SCCM/MECM, Group Policy (DISM / PowerShell), PowerShell (`Add-AppxPackage`).
Add-AppxPackage -Path "\\fileserver\apps\MyApp_1.0.0.0_x64.msix"
Add-AppxProvisionedPackage -Online `
-PackagePath "MyApp_1.0.0.0_x64.msix" `

App Installer XML controls update checks (launch/background), prompts, activation blocking, background tasks, check interval (`HoursBetweenUpdateChecks`, 0 = every launch), and downgrade policy (`ForceUpdateFromAnyVersion`). Custom update logic: `Package.Current.CheckUpdateAvailabilityAsync()`. Differential updates download changed blocks automatically when the same `PackageName` and `Publisher` are used.
